The shop closed in May 2025 and will reopen under the ownership of Tim and Deanna Green, who plan to renovate and update the space while preserving its tradition. The legendary shop originally opened in 1980 and was founded by Patricia Green, who was inducted into the International Candy Hall of Fame in 2010.

The Chocolate Tree is a historic confectionery shop that closed in May 2025 and will reopen under new ownership this fall. Tim and Deanna Green, with Tim being the eldest son of founder Patricia Green, will renovate and update the space while preserving signature recipes and traditions. Plans include reviving "all-you-can-eat" chocolate nights, introducing chocolate-making classes, and expanding into online sales, though an official reopening date has not been announced.

data.status: hoping to open his location around mid-July
data.short_description: Wing Snob is a chicken wing chain known for freshly made wings and signature sauces including Lemon Pepper, Awesome Sauce, Garlic Parm, and Buffalo. Franchisee Johnny Shabani is hoping to open at 336 W Chrysler Drive in Belvidere around mid-July, sharing the building with a Dunkin'. Shabani has been planning the location since November 2024 and signed the lease at the beginning of 2026.

Dandee Donut Factory is a Florida-based donut and diner-style franchise serving fresh donuts, all-day breakfast, and family-friendly comfort food. The Revere, Massachusetts location announced its closure on June 7 in a Facebook post, with no specific reason provided for the closure. The company continues to operate restaurants in South Florida in Pompano Beach, Deerfield Beach, and Margate.

data.store_name: Unnamed brasserie (Eugene Remm / Catch & Shoot LLC)
data.short_description: A yet-to-be-named upscale French brasserie concept is planned by Eugene Remm of Catch Hospitality Group for the former Saint Theo's space at 340 Bleecker St. in the West Village. The filing with Community Board 2 describes the concept as a "sun-kissed" New York-influenced take on the classic French brasserie, with seating for 92 guests including 13 bar seats and sidewalk café seating. A full liquor license is being sought via the filing associated with Catch & Shoot LLC.

Prospect Five Points is a wine bar and restaurant that served Jacksonville's Riverside community for nearly five years. The restaurant announced its permanent closure on Instagram, citing a "rough year" with a difficult slow season and reduced staffing, and confirmed it shut down operations on June 28, 2026. The final day of service will include a cabaret show with six acts, with seating beginning at 6 p.m. and performances at 7 p.m.

data.status: expected to open in the fall of 2026
data.short_description: G&G Surf Club is a new seafood-focused restaurant concept from Chef Troy Guard's TAG Restaurant Group, featuring a raw bar, open kitchen, and spacious patio. The restaurant has secured a lease at 8100 E. Union Ave. in the Denver Tech Center and is expected to open in the fall of 2026. The concept celebrates Guard's coastal culinary influences from Hawaii, Seattle, and San Diego, while incorporating prime steaks and wood-fired preparations.

Paris Bistro is a French restaurant that served South Naperville for 13 years as an independent, family-owned business. The restaurant confirmed its permanent closure on June 7 through a Facebook post, with no reason cited in the announcement. According to a Chicago Tribune report, the owners took on pandemic-era loans during COVID-19, and accumulated debt and rent arrears made reorganization impossible.

Pure Green is a health and wellness franchise serving cold-pressed juices, smoothies, and açaí bowls, founded in 2014 by Ross Franklin and now operating more than 150 locations across 25-plus states. Franchise owners Carson Saleumsy and Sean Hasher are targeting a late-summer opening at 1700 N. Front St. in Philadelphia's Fishtown neighborhood, with construction currently underway. In Pennsylvania, Pure Green also operates stores in Langhorne and Wilkes-Barre, with an additional location planned for Ardmore.

data.status: served its final day on June 6
data.short_description: Alara is a high-end restaurant positioned as a $6.5 million "crown jewel" in the Madison Square development on the Medpace campus in Madisonville. The restaurant served its final day on June 6, closing after just two years in operation with no official reason provided for the sudden shutdown. Reservations were reportedly canceled with guests directed to the nearby restaurant Zingaro.

Lorena Mediterranean Brasserie is a coastal Mediterranean concept developed by Fabio Viviani Hospitality, centered around open-fire cooking and shareable dishes including wood-grilled fish, whole-roasted vegetables, and steak frites. The restaurant is scheduled to open in late 2026, taking over the former Alara space at 5410 Medpace Way in the Madison Square development. Celebrity chef Fabio Viviani, known for appearances on Top Chef and multiple Food Network programs, leads the hospitality group that also operates Zingaro within the same development.

ARLA is a rooftop restaurant on the sixth floor of 15 E. Oak Street in Chicago's Gold Coast neighborhood, combining Mediterranean and Japanese flavors with views of Lake Michigan and the city skyline. The 8,500-square-foot restaurant will open on June 18, featuring terracotta plaster walls, walnut woodwork, polished brass accents, and private and semi-private dining rooms. The space was designed by LG Group and Offshoot Creative, with Chef/Partner Soo Ahn leading the culinary vision.

data.status: preparing to open in Downtown Columbus later this summer
data.short_description: The Line is a forthcoming full-service restaurant from nonprofit organization Service!, operating in a former Columbus College of Art & Design building while also serving as a workforce training ground for hospitality professionals. The restaurant is preparing to open later this summer at 145 N. Grant Ave. in Downtown Columbus, with chef Matthew Heaggans leading the kitchen as executive chef. The Line plans to employ approximately eight full-time staff while welcoming cohorts of paid trainees, and has partnered with Otterbein University and Columbus State Community College for educational certifications.

Domo Sushi Kitchen & Bar is a Japanese cuisine restaurant originally opened in Columbus' Short North neighborhood in 2023, known for a contemporary approach to sushi. A second location is planned for Historic Dublin at 12 E Bridge St, taking over the former Mr. Sushi space at the corner of Bridge Street and High Street. Owner Daniel Kim noted the location holds special significance as Mr. Sushi was previously owned and operated by his father.

data.status: targeting an opening ahead of the upcoming college football season
data.short_description: Atomic Wings is a Buffalo-inspired chicken wing chain serving wings, tenders, sandwiches, and sauces. The franchise is heading to 2112 N. High St. in Columbus's University Gateway North building, targeting an opening before the college football season, though the project is currently in the design and planning stages. Founded in 1989, Atomic Wings has grown to more than 30 locations across 11 states and will serve 100% halal, antibiotic- and hormone-free chicken.

data.status: aiming for a July opening date
data.short_description: Osteria Gilberto is a new Italian concept being developed by owner Sergio Barbone. It is coming to 1224 W Webster Avenue in Lincoln Park, with the owner aiming for a July opening date. Barbone also owns Bakehouse Chicago, with bakery locations in Lakeview, Roscoe Village, and Southport.

Le Petit Comptoir Wine & Cheese is a wine-and-cheese concept featuring small plates, charcuterie boards, grilled cheeses, and zero-proof options in a cozy setting. Owner Alex Lewis is tentatively targeting a July 2026 opening beside Marblehead House of Pizza at 1 Atlantic Ave, though the timeline depends on final preparations and hiring. Lewis has already been building excitement through weekly wine-and-cheese tastings, pairing events, and educational classes ahead of the grand opening.

The Laureate is a new boutique hotel being developed by Tina McCarthy in partnership with Chad Ingram and Rob Johnston, incorporating the historic Farmers and Merchants Bank Building at 167 Laurens St. along with adjacent property on Park Ave. The project will break ground this fall and will include a four-story structure with 84 rooms, suites, and extended-stay residences, plus a lobby bar and garden courtyard. The historic bank building will house a restaurant and bar, meeting rooms, fitness space, and possibly a small spa.
